newsitem.title: GERMANY: Berlin right-wing jobs protest ends in clashes.
newsitem.headline: Berlin right-wing jobs protest ends in clashes.

text.p: Several people were injured on Saturday in the eastern side of Berlin when right-wing youths protesting to "keep jobs for the Germans" clashed with left-wing groups, German police said.
A spokesman for police said some youths had been detained in the Hellersdorf district of the city where the clashes took place, but he declined to give any further details.
About 50 rightwingers had gathered at a suburban train station in a demonstration to protest against foreigners taking jobs away from Germans.

About 500 leftwingers, including members of the federation of Jewish students, the German DGB trade union federation, the reform communist PDS party and Turkish groups, staged a counter-demonstration.
Some of them ended up brawling with the rightists.

The clashes came as a sign of growing social unrest amid soaring unemployment and warnings from trade unions that jobless figures which hit a new post-World War Two low of 4.66 million in January could get even worse.
